title: ESO’s Paranal Observatory by night
caption: Comet Lovejoy, the Moon and a laser over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Night has fallen over ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile's Atacama Desert. Comet Lovejoy hangs low on the horizon, just right of the Moon. One of the giant Unit Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope (VLT) fires a reddish laser beam upward, and above it a satellite has left a streak across the sky.

The laser creates an artificial star that helps astronomers make sharper observations. ESO describes the VLT as the world's most advanced visible-light astronomical observatory. The photograph was taken on 22 December 2011.

Cerro Paranal is a mountain 2600 metres high, about 130 km south of Antofagasta and 12 km from the Pacific coast, in one of the world's driest regions. The clear view of the Milky Way's stars here shows how good its observing conditions are.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based night photograph by G. Brammer; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the comet and the Milky Way may look more distinct here than to someone standing on the mountain.
